title: Blackened Cod Taco Night
seoTitle: Blackened Cod Taco Night | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Spice-crusted cod with lime slaw and avocado crema in corn tortillas
subtitle: Spice-crusted cod with lime slaw and avocado crema in corn tortillas
description: Cod fillets crust with blackening spice in a hot skillet, then tuck into corn tortillas with cabbage slaw and avocado crema.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Blackened Cod Taco Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch fish. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix blackening spice
steps.instruction: Combine paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne, 1 tbsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper. Rub should smell smoky and evenly blended. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep slaw and crema
steps.instruction: Toss cabbage with half the lime juice and pinch of salt until lightly wilted but still crunchy. Blend avocado, yogurt, and remaining lime for crema. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Coat and sear cod
steps.instruction: Pat cod dry, coat generously with blackening spice. Sear in hot oiled skillet 3–4 minutes per side until crust is dark and fish reads 145°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and flake fish
steps.instruction: Rest fish 3 minutes, break into large chunks. Flesh should be opaque, moist, and flake cleanly without drying into strings. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F until flakes separate. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Assemble tacos
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas in foil. Fill with fish, slaw, and crema. Crust should stay spicy and crisp-tender, not soggy from over-filling. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Do not move fish early—crust releases when properly seared.
Reduce cayenne for mild crews; offer hot sauce at the line instead.
leftovers: Fish over rice bowl with slaw and crema.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Big spice and fresh crunch. Handheld format keeps service moving when everyone hits the kitchen at once.
mealPrepNotes: Mix blackening spice in bulk. Pat cod dry right before cooking. Station: Vent hood on—blackening spice smokes at high heat. Station: Cook fish in batches in cast iron for best crust. Station: Taco bar: fish, slaw, crema, pico, lime, hot sauce.
